Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:9: "Watchfulness" [zehirut] - the Torah uses this word in three senses. The first, in Parashat Yitro, in the words of Yitro to Moses (Exodus 18:20), "and you shall warn them of the statutes and the laws" - and they explained, of blessed memory, in Keritot, chapter "Amru Lo" (13b), on the verse (Leviticus 10:11), "and to teach the children of Israel all the statutes," and so on, that "statutes" [chukkim] are the midrashim - and similarly we shall expound this verse, that "statutes" are the midrashim. And "the laws" [torot] is the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. And he says "you shall warn" - it appears that just as a warning is needed for a negative commandment, so a warning is needed for a positive commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:10: The second sense is found in the Prophets, especially many times in Ezekiel (Ezekiel 3:19), "and you, because you warned the wicked," and so on - and this is the essential warning concerning a negative commandment, relevant to the exposition of the discourse before us, "and you shall keep yourself from every evil thing, that a person not think by day," and so on, "from here Rabbi Pinchas said, watchfulness" - behold, that watchfulness is guarding.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:11: Further, this word is used in Scripture even for a minor precision, in what King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 19:11), "more desirable than gold," and so on, "and sweeter than honey," and so on, "also Your servant is warned by them" - and it is explained in the Idra of Ha'azinu (page 295b) that this is said of the letters gimel, yud, chaf, kuf [the palatal letters], for of the palate it is said, "his palate is sweetness" - and King David, peace be upon him, was careful [nizhar] with these letters to pronounce them correctly in their articulation, in these words: gimel-yud-chaf-kuf (Job 6:6), "can that which is unsavory be eaten without salt," and so on, and it is written (Isaiah 32:17), "and the work of righteousness shall be peace," "more desirable than gold, than much fine gold, and sweeter," and so on - "sweeter," certainly; King David said, "also Your servant is warned by them" - I testify concerning myself that every day I was careful with them, not to err in them even for a single day - to this point. And from this we derive that in all the precise distinctions written in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, and in the books of the pious, one must be careful in all of them not to stumble in any of them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:12: It follows that the word "watchfulness" includes both the fulfillment of a positive deed and the fulfillment of a warning concerning a negative commandment, whether written in the Torah or in the words of the Scribes - such as not gazing at a woman, even at her garments spread out on a wall, and many similar things. And it is possible that because this word is all-inclusive, it was not counted in the Yerushalmi (Shabbat, chapter 1, halachah 3) among the levels of the attributes - rather it says, alacrity brings one to cleanliness, cleanliness brings one to purity, purity brings one to holiness. And so they did not count separation among the attributes, because separation and holiness are equivalent in their matter, as we shall explain, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:13: "Alacrity" [zerizut] is an attribute superior to the previous one, touching both positive and negative commandments - to be watchful and swift in a positive commandment, that if a commandment comes into his hand he does it immediately, as it is said (Exodus 12:17), "and you shall observe the matzot [ha-matzot]" - and they expounded in the Mechilta (Parashah 9): do not read "ha-matzot" but "ha-mitzvot" [the commandments] - just as one does not let the matzah become leavened [chametz], so one should not let a commandment become "leavened" [delayed] - rather, if a commandment comes into your hand, do it at once - to this point. And so they also expounded in the Mechilta on the verse (Joshua 3:1), "and Joshua rose early in the morning" - this teaches that the alacritous rise early for commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:14: And the attribute of alacrity indicates the desire of his soul and heart to do that thing out of love for the Creator, and therefore he hastens and does not delay, as the Tanna said (Avot, chapter 5, mishnah 20), concerning the attribute of alacrity: be bold as a leopard, light as an eagle, swift as a deer, and mighty as a lion, to do the will of your Father in Heaven. And when a person does the thing with alacrity and joy, a new spirit and a spiritual spirit of life is added to him, in such a way that he becomes light as an eagle - and this matter depends on removing from his heart the spirit of laziness and sadness, which is the external force that weighs down all a person's limbs, so that he has no strength to rise from his place, neither to read nor to perform a commandment, as though all his limbs were dead. And if a person arouses his heart and removes the external force of laziness from upon him, by cleaving to the desire of love of the LORD, who is the source of life, then his heart is alive, and he reads, studies, and performs his commandments with alacrity and joy to do the will of his Father in Heaven - and then strength is added to him to be light as an eagle, mighty as a lion, and so on. Concerning this it is said (Isaiah 40:31), "but those who wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength," and so on, "they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:15: And the general rule is that there is no alacrity except through the desire of love, and therefore it is among the levels that lead to piety, which is love, as explained. And along these lines they explained, of blessed memory, in Bereshit Rabbah (55:8), on the verse (Genesis 22:3), "and Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey" - Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: love upsets the [normal] order - did he not have servants? Rather, love upsets the order - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:16: And without doubt, "and Abraham rose early in the morning" is alacrity, along the lines of "and Joshua rose early in the morning," as expounded, and it is from the side of love - and from the side of love he upset the order.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:17: And in the book Beit Middot he wrote concerning the attribute of alacrity, in these words: know, my sons, that the virtue of alacrity is an important attribute, for from the very beginning of man's creation he was created only to be alert in his deeds and his ways, along the lines of what is said (Genesis 2:7), "and man became a living soul [nefesh chayah]" - what is "chayah"? Alacrity. He was made a poor servant to himself, that if he does not toil he does not eat. See what is written concerning this (ibid. 2:15), "and He placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to keep it" - and did it need working and keeping? Rather, it was in order to make him alert - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:18: And behold, according to what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Bereshit Rabbah, that "to work it and to keep it" refers to the occupation with Torah and commandments, it follows that alacrity is to occupy oneself with Torah and commandments. They said in Bereshit Rabbah: "and He placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to keep it" - lest you say there is labor in the Garden of Eden to dig and till the soil, but do not all the trees grow of themselves? Or lest you say there is labor in the Garden of Eden to water the garden, but does not a river go out from Eden to water the garden? Rather, "to work it and to keep it" means to occupy oneself with words of Torah and to keep its commandments, as it is said (Genesis 3:24), "to keep the way to the tree of life," along the lines of (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:19: And in the Idra of Naso (page 141b), on the verse (Genesis 2:7), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul" - he said: "and the LORD God formed man" - who is male and female - "dust from the ground" - image within image, form within form, and why all this? In order to draw forth and gaze through it into the concealed of the supernal concealed, to the end of all concealment. This is what is written, "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" - the soul upon which all life above and below depend, and through which they exist. "And man became a living soul" - to cleave and enter into repairs in this manner, and to draw that soul from level to level to the end of all levels (variant: concealments), so that that soul be found in everything and spread through everything, so as to be one alone. And whoever cuts this off from the world is as one who cuts off this soul, and gives the appearance that there is another soul besides this - and therefore he and his memory shall be cut off for all generations.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:20: Behold, the matter of "living soul" is said, above, in Atzilut, concerning the secret of the supernal life that spreads from the Cause over all to all existing things, which is the breath of life for all the worlds - and correspondingly, in this reality, man below has within him the breath of life, and when he is cleaved to his God in the secret of the supernal life, alacrity and a new spirit are given to him, and his heart and limbs come alive to do the will of his Owner, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:21: And behold, one who is cleaved to the attribute of alacrity is cleaved to "a woman of valor," "a woman who fears the LORD," in whom is the essence of all alacrity, as Solomon, peace be upon him, mentioned in her praise (Proverbs 31:15), "she rises while it is yet night, and gives food to her household," and so on, "she girds her loins with strength, and strengthens her arms" (ibid. 31:17), "she makes linen garments and sells them" (ibid. 31:24), "she looks well to the ways of her household, and does not eat the bread of idleness" (ibid. 31:27). Behold, it is explicit that all her attributes are in alacrity, and there is no "bread of idleness" in her, for the bread of idleness is on the outside - "this too, corresponding to that, God has made" (Ecclesiastes 7:14).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:22: And the further reason is that performing the commandment with alacrity indicates that he performs it with joy, and it is written (Psalms 100:2), "serve the LORD with joy" - and it is known what they explained, of blessed memory (Shabbat 30b): the Shechinah rests only from within joy, and not from within sadness and laughter - it follows that through his performing it with alacrity and joy, the Shechinah rests upon him; but one who performs it out of laziness and sadness is punished, as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the LORD," and so on, "with joy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:23: And the explanation of "and does not eat the bread of idleness": "bread" refers to the food of the commandment, or the Torah brought near to it, for the commandments are called "delicacies" [mat'amim], as they explained in the Zohar (Tikkunei Zohar 51a), "and make me delicacies such as I love" (Genesis 27:4), from the positive commandments; and so of the Torah it is said (Proverbs 9:5), "come, eat of my bread." And when a person performs them out of laziness, she [the Shechinah] does not eat them as is fitting - concerning her it is said (Deuteronomy 4:24), "for the LORD your God is a consuming fire," and her eating is Torah and the commandments, as explained above - and since she does not eat them, they are cast outside.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:24: And therefore, one must very, very much cleave to alacrity and not to laziness. Concerning alacrity it is said (Proverbs 22:29), "do you see a man diligent [mahir] in his work" - meaning, diligent in the work of the Shechinah, in which there is work, as they explained in the Tikkunim (page 14b); and her work, meaning her repair, is the performance of Torah and commandments - and whoever holds fast to her with alacrity, "he shall stand before kings," for within her the ten kings are included, as explained in the Tikkunim - "he shall not stand before obscure men [choshechim]," who are the husks, which are darkness and not light. And from the affirmative you infer the negative: whoever holds fast, Heaven forfend, to laziness, is cleaved to obscure men and separates himself from the supernal angels of holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:25: And it says "he shall stand" [yityatzev], not "he shall sit" - for standing [yetzivah] is from a standing position, and it is known that all standing in the world is [associated with] the male (Zohar, Parashat Tetzaveh, page 183a) - and the matter is that through his holding fast to the Shechinah in the secret of the arousal of female waters through alacrity in the commandments, as explained, he raises her, through her, to the world of the male.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:26: Further, it is possible [to explain] "yityatzev," along the lines of what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in the Mechilta on the verse (Exodus 14:13), "stand still and see the salvation of the LORD," and so too on the verse (ibid. 15:20), "and Miriam the prophetess took" - that "standing" everywhere refers to the holy spirit, in these words: "stand still and see" - Israel said to him, when? He said to them, today the Shechinah, the holy spirit, rested upon you - for "standing" everywhere means only the holy spirit, as it is said (Amos 9:1), "I saw the LORD standing upon the altar, and He said, strike the capital," and it says (1 Samuel 3:10), "and the LORD came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel," and it says (Deuteronomy 31:14), "call Joshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Meeting," and it says (Exodus 2:4), "and his sister stood [vatetatzav] afar off" - and the holy spirit rested upon her - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:27: And on the verse "and Miriam the prophetess took," they explained that the verse "and his sister stood afar off" is the most conclusive of all, for "afar off," yet knowing what would happen - all indicate the holy spirit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:28: And in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, beginning of page 301), they explained that Malchut is called "the holy spirit" when she nurses from the secret of Chochmah, and she is the spirit that nurses from the supernal holiness, which is Chochmah - and therefore the word "yetzivah" [standing] is fitting for her in the aspect of the holy spirit. And it follows from this that alacrity is a level that leads to the holy spirit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:29: And it is possible to say it another way. We find that they explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Kedoshim, page 82a) that in Tiferet too there is alacrity, in that it acts from Abba and Imma immediately, without any mixture, in these words: and Israel, who are called sons, in general "son" and "daughter" from the side of Tiferet and Malchut, who are son and daughter - the honor of their father and mother, to perform His command; and His command is the positive commandments, and the masters of the Mishnah have already established, "there is one who is commanded and does it," and therefore it is "we shall do and we shall hear" - and this is the honor of Abba and Imma, who commanded their son to do so, and he does it at once, without any delay at all - to this point. And along these lines it is explained in Chochmah, and we copied it in the Gate of Fear, end of chapter 2.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:30: And in the Tikkunim, in Tikkun 39 (page 79b), they explained that Tiferet and Yesod, each one, is called "commanded and does it," in the commandments included in the Shechinah - and according to this, the alacritous person holds fast to the level of the world of the male, and therefore "he shall stand before kings," as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:31: And in any case, the essence of alacrity is in the place of the deed, and depends on it, for it serves the whole of Atzilut - and for this reason, the princes, because they were lazy in the donation for the Tabernacle, the letter yud, which is the Shechinah, was missing from them, as it is said (Exodus 36:27), "and the princes [ha-nesi'im] brought" - "ha-nesi'im" is written lacking the yud - and the reason is as explained, that "she does not eat the bread of idleness." And I heard from the mouth of my teacher, peace be upon him, that for their repair, they brought at the dedication of the princes ten things - one silver bowl, one basin, and so on - you find there ten things - and "ha-nesi'im" is written full, with a yud - they hastened to bring this to counter the laziness by which they had blemished the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:32: And know further, that alacrity is acquired in a person's soul only from fear, for one who fears the king is alert to perform his command, and fears lest a fault be found in him afterward, and therefore he hastens in the performance of Torah and commandments. And so, for this reason, alacrity is fitting in the Shechinah, for there is where fear resides; and likewise cleanliness and purity are also branches of fear, for one must fear lest his garments be soiled before the king, but rather clean and pure - and so one must cleanse and purify his limbs and his soul, since he stands always before the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed and exalted be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:33: Further, concerning the attribute of alacrity, I found several particulars written in a manuscript book, and I saw fit to copy them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:34: "Cleanliness" [nekiyut] is used in four senses. The first, cleanliness and purity from iniquity and transgression, as it says (Numbers 5:31), "then the man shall be clean from iniquity," and "cleanse me from great transgression" (Psalms 19:14).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:35: This attribute is necessary for piety, which is love, for it is impossible, while there is a blemish in the soul, for love to cleave to it. And it is like the parable of a garment upon which oil or some other stain has fallen - it will not accept any dye until it is washed and that stain removed from it. So too, while the soul is soiled with the stains of its iniquities, if it does not cleanse and wash itself through repentance - and a particular repentance for each and every sin, as will be explained - it will not cleave lastingly to the supernal spirituality, for the iniquity is a partition separating between it and its God; and therefore alien thoughts will confuse him while he stands occupied with Torah or prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:36: And in the Yerushalmi they brought proof that alacrity leads to cleanliness, for it is written (Leviticus 16:20), "and when he has finished [ve-chilah] atoning" - the matter being that "ve-chilah" indicates alacrity, because its meaning is completing the matter, and because the word "ve-chilah" is superfluous there, in Parashat Acharei Mot, concerning the service of the Day of Atonement - for what need was there to say "ve-chilah"? Let it say "and he shall atone" [ve-chiper] - rather, the intent is certainly to speak of alacrity. And it says "mi-kaper" - the word "kapparah" [atonement] means cleansing, purification, and this is a word in the Aramaic language. And so Rashi, peace be upon him, explained in Tractate Chullin (8b) concerning a knife with which a torn animal was slaughtered, where he said there: and if there is a worn cloth to "le-mikhparei" it, it is unnecessary - and Rashi explained: "bilta" is a worn piece; "de-farsa," as we translate "the covering of the doorway" as "parsa"; "le-mikhparei" - to wipe it. And its counterpart in Gittin, concerning Nebuzaradan, "and he wished to wipe his hands [le-kapurei]" on that man; and in the Temple courtyard, the sprinkling basins are called "keforei zahav," golden basins, for one wipes his finger of blood [into them] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:37: And behold, the word "kapparah" means purification and the wiping away of the stain from the garment, such that no soiling remains in it at all; and so too concerning the purification of iniquity spoken of in terms of cleanliness [nekiyut], the meaning of "kapparah" is the concealing of the stain of that iniquity from the soul. But when purification of iniquity is spoken of in terms of "taharah" [purity], as he says (Psalms 51:4), "and purify me from my sin" - "taharah" is the fine bleaching of the garment - and this is what Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "tahor" - bright and refined, superior to "clean." And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, also explained (Berachot 15a) concerning "I will wash my hands in cleanliness" (ibid. 26:6), "with whatever cleanses" - but "taharah" is with water that purifies and bleaches things well.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:38: And the reason purity is needed after cleanliness may be understood from what Scripture says (Leviticus 13:58), "and the garment, or the warp, or the woof, or whatever thing of skin it be, which you shall wash, if the plague has departed from them, then it shall be washed a second time, and it shall be pure" - and the second washing is to give it a spirituality of holiness and purity, for when the plague departs from it, it remains without impurity but also without purity, and to give it the spirituality of purity a second washing is needed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:39: Further, it is possible to explain the reason for the second washing this way: even though the plague has already departed - for the plague is a force among the forces of Lilith, from whose side come the four appearances of plagues, as explained in the Tikkunim - and when it cleaves to a person or to his other vessels, it is cleaved in such a way that it does not separate quickly, but the imprint of the impurity remains there, even though it is not visible to the eyes; and it is still recognizable, in that place where the plague was, that it rested there - and therefore, "it shall be washed a second time."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:40: And this is an additional virtue of holiness over impurity - for holiness, wherever it rests, never departs from there, as they explained, of blessed memory (Megillah, chapter 3, mishnah 3), concerning a synagogue that has fallen into ruin, that one does not eulogize within it, and so on, as it is said (Leviticus 26:31), "and I will bring your sanctuaries to desolation" - in their holiness they remain, even when desolate. But the matter of impurity, even though it is spiritual, through a second washing it is purified and bleached, and that husk is utterly nullified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:41: And so too concerning repentance: even though a person has abandoned the sin completely, and regretted it, and does not return at all to his former deed, and purified himself through self-affliction - this does not suffice for him until the Accuser does not recognize it in him at all, as though he had no iniquity at all; rather, "it shall be washed a second time, and it shall be pure," as though he had never sinned at all. And this is what they said in the Yerushalmi, cleanliness leads to purity, as it is said (Leviticus 12:8), "and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be pure [tahor]" - and what need is there for purity after atonement? Rather, atonement is cleanliness and not purity itself, and therefore purity is needed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:42: Further, we find a second meaning to cleanliness [nekiyut], in what Scripture says regarding Abimelech (Genesis 20:5), "in the integrity of my heart and the cleanliness of my hands," and so too (Psalms 24:4), "clean hands and a pure heart" - one must strive to purify his hands from every large matter and from everything that blemishes with the hands, as will be explained, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:43: And some of these are explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayera, page 100b) in the interpretation of the verse "clean hands," and so on, in these words: come and see, "who shall ascend the mountain of the LORD" - and afterward he returns and explains "clean hands," that he does not perform sorcery with his hands, and does not become powerful through them, as is unnecessary, and further, that he does not become defiled through them nor defile his body through them, like those who defile themselves with their hands to become impure - and this is "clean hands."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:44: The third [meaning] is what is said concerning the children of Gad and the children of Reuben (Numbers 32:22), "and you shall be clean before the LORD and before Israel" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, learned from here that a person must distance himself from suspicion, as we learn (Shekalim, chapter 3, mishnah 2): the one who removes the terumah [from the Temple chamber] does not enter with a hem-bordered cloak, nor with shoes, nor with sandals, lest he become poor and they say, from the sin of the chamber he became poor; or lest he become rich and they say, from the terumah of the chamber he became rich - for a person must satisfy people just as he must satisfy the Omnipresent, as it is said, "and you shall be clean before the LORD and before Israel," and it says (Proverbs 3:4), "and find favor and good understanding in the eyes of God and man." And along these lines is what they said, of blessed memory (Chullin 44b): distance yourself from what is unseemly and from what resembles it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:45: Further, a fourth interpretation is found in the verse (Job 4:7), "remember now, who ever perished being innocent [naki]" - and they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 215b) that this refers to Pinchas, who was zealous for the covenant and did not defile himself with the sin of Peor with the daughters of Moab. And from this we derive that "clean" [naki] is the attribute of the righteous [tzaddik], and therefore Pinchas was given the covenant of peace, as it is said (Numbers 25:12), "therefore behold, I give to him My covenant of peace." And so we find these two words together (Exodus 23:7), "and the innocent and righteous [ve-naki ve-tzaddik] you shall not slay" - showing that they are both one matter. And regarding the "cleanliness" mentioned in the discourse, the meaning is that he desires to be clean from anything that blemishes the sign of the covenant, which is in the Righteous One [Yesod], in such a way that he can be called "clean" in this attribute.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:46: "Cleanliness leads to purity" - although purity has already been explained under the word "cleanliness," nevertheless there is still more to explain, along the lines of what we expounded concerning the previous words. "Purity" is found in the Torah, Prophets, and Writings in many senses; but the one relevant to practical matters is this: the first, purity through immersion in forty se'ah [of water], as is found many times in the Torah - among them (Leviticus 22:4), "any man of the seed of Aaron," and so on, "shall not eat until he is pure [yit'har]." And likewise, "and shall be unclean until evening, and then shall be pure," and so on (Leviticus 11:32); "and he shall bathe his flesh in living water, and be pure" (Leviticus 15:13) - and this is said of the zav, for whom the Torah required living water.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:47: Behold, purity through immersion is a great aid for a person's soul to cleave to his God and His service - for while he is impure, the impurity dulls a person's heart, as explained above, of blessed memory, on "and you shall be defiled by them" (Leviticus 11:43).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:48: And the essence of love and cleaving depends on the purity of the heart from alien thoughts, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 51:12), "create in me a pure heart, O God" - and so Rabbenu Tam, peace be upon him, wrote in Sefer HaYashar (chapter 13), that the purity of the body renews purity in the soul. And when the body is impure, certainly some blemish reaches the soul, and it is impossible for him to direct his intention properly without some other thought confusing him and separating him from the supernal root - for he is separated because of the blemish in his soul, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 52b), that He does not rest upon a blemished soul, as it is written (Leviticus 21:18), "anyone who has a blemish shall not draw near." And therefore it is impossible for him to have cleaving, for the essence of cleaving is to the Cause of causes, the soul of all souls - and since He, may He be exalted, does not rest upon him, how can he be cleaved to Him?
